title: द्वादशोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Dhritarashtra asks how Arjuna fought the Samshaptakas and others, and Sanjaya describes the heroic warriors on both sides advancing. Krishna and Arjuna advance against the Samshaptakas as the two armies clash like the planets.
summary.kn: ಅರ್ಜುನ ಸಂಶಪ್ತಕರು ಮತ್ತು ಇತರರೊಡನೆ ಹೇಗೆ ಹೋರಾಡಿದನೆಂದು ಧೃತರಾಷ್ಟ್ರ ಕೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಎರಡೂ ಕಡೆಯ ವೀರರ ಮುನ್ನಡೆಯನ್ನು ಸಂಜಯ ವರ್ಣಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಕೃಷ್ಣ-ಅರ್ಜುನರು ಸಂಶಪ್ತಕರ ಮೇಲೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತಾರೆ; ಸೈನ್ಯಗಳು ಗ್ರಹಗಳಂತೆ ಸಂಧಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.
summary.hi: धृतराष्ट्र पूछते हैं कि अर्जुन ने संशप्तकों और अन्य से कैसे युद्ध किया, और संजय दोनों पक्षों के वीरों के बढ़ने का वर्णन करते हैं। कृष्ण-अर्जुन संशप्तकों की ओर बढ़ते हैं और सेनाएँ ग्रहों की तरह भिड़ती हैं।
summary.te: అర్జునుడు సంశప్తకులు ఇతరులతో ఎలా పోరాడాడని ధృతరాష్ట్రుడు అడుగుతాడు; ఇరుపక్షాల వీరులు ముందుకు సాగడాన్ని సంజయుడు వర్ణిస్తాడు. కృష్ణార్జునులు సంశప్తకులపైకి వెళతారు; సేనలు గ్రహాల్లా ఢీకొంటాయి.
summary.ta: அர்ஜுனன் சம்சப்தகர் முதலியோருடன் எவ்வாறு போரிட்டான் என்று த்ருதராஷ்டிரன் கேட்க, இரு தரப்பு வீரரின் முன்னேற்றத்தைச் சஞ்சயன் விவரிக்கிறான். கண்ணனும் அர்ஜுனனும் சம்சப்தகரை நோக்கிச் செல்ல, படைகள் கோள்கள் போல் மோதுகின்றன.
summary.ml: സംശപ്തകരെയും മറ്റുള്ളവരെയും അർജുനൻ എങ്ങനെ നേരിട്ടു എന്ന് ധൃതരാഷ്ട്രർ ചോദിക്കുന്നു; ഇരുപക്ഷത്തെയും വീര യോദ്ധാക്കൾ മുന്നേറുന്നത് സഞ്ജയൻ വിവരിക്കുന്നു. ഗ്രഹങ്ങൾ കൂട്ടിമുട്ടുംപോലെ ഇരുസേനകളും ഏറ്റുമുട്ടുമ്പോൾ, കൃഷ്ണനും അർജുനനും സംശപ്തകർക്കെതിരെ മുന്നേറുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 8.12; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 29 2019

verses.text: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच

meaning.en: Dhritarashtra said:

verses.text:
यथा संशप्तकैः सार्धमर्जुनस्याभवद्रणः ।
अन्येषां च मदीयानां पाण्डवैस्तद्ब्रवीहि मे ॥

meaning.en: Tell me how Arjuna's battle with the Samshaptakas went, and what happened between the Pandavas and others of my side.

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
शृणु राजन्यथावृत्तं संग्रामं ब्रुवतो मम ।
वीराणां शत्रुभिः सार्धं देहपाप्मप्रणाशनम् ॥

meaning.en: Listen, O king, as I tell you exactly how the battle of the heroes with their enemies went, that which destroys the sin of the body.

verses.text:
पार्थः संशप्तकगणं प्रविश्यार्णवसंनिभम् ।
व्यक्षोभयदमित्रघ्नो महावात इवार्णवम् ॥

meaning.en: Partha, slayer of foes, entering the band of Samshaptakas, vast as an ocean, churned it like a great wind churning the sea.

verses.text:
शिरांस्युन्मथ्य वीराणां शितैर्भल्लैर्धनंजयः ।
पूर्णचन्द्राभवक्त्राणि स्वक्षिभ्रूदशनानि च ।
संतस्तार क्षितिं क्षिप्रं विनालैर्नलिनैरिव ॥

meaning.en: Dhananjaya, tearing off the heads of heroes with sharp bhallas, faces like the full moon with fine eyes, brows and teeth, quickly strewed the ground with them like lotuses without stalks.

verses.text:
सुवृत्तानायतान्पुष्टांश्चन्दनागुरुभूषितान् ।
सायुधान्सतनुत्राणान्पञ्चास्योरगसंनिभान् ।
बाहून्क्षुरैरमित्राणां विचकर्तार्जुनो रणे ॥

meaning.en: Arjuna in the battle cut off with razor-edged arrows the arms of his enemies, well rounded, long and sturdy, adorned with sandal and aloe, bearing weapons and armour, like five-hooded serpents.

verses.text:
धुर्यान्धुर्यतरान्सूतान्ध्वजांश्चापानि सायकान् ।
पाणीनरत्नीनसकृद्भल्लैश्चिच्छेद पाण्डवः ॥

meaning.en: The Pandava with bhallas repeatedly cut down yoke-horses and better horses, charioteers, banners, bows, arrows, hands and arms.

verses.text:
द्विपान्हयान्रथांश्चैव सारोहानर्जुनो रणे ।
शरैरनेकसाहस्रै राजन्निन्ये यमक्षयम् ॥

meaning.en: In the battle, Arjuna with many thousands of arrows sent elephants, horses and chariots with their riders to Yama's abode, O king.

verses.text:
तं प्रवीरं प्रतीयाता नर्दमाना इवर्षभाः ।
वाशितार्थमभिक्रुद्धा हुंकृत्वा चाभिदुद्रुवुः ।
निघ्नन्तमभिजघ्नुस्ते शरैः शृङ्गैरिवर्षभाः ॥

meaning.en: Charging at that hero like bellowing bulls, furious over a cow in season, they shouted and ran at him; as he struck them, they struck him with arrows, as bulls do with horns.

verses.text:
तस्य तेषां च तद्युद्धमभवल्लोमहर्षणम् ।
त्रैलोक्यविजये यादृग्दैत्यानां सह वज्रिणा ॥

meaning.en: The battle between him and them was hair-raising, like the battle of the Daityas with the thunderbolt-wielder over the conquest of the three worlds.

verses.text:
अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य द्विषतां सर्वतोऽर्जुनः ।
इषुभिर्बहुभिस्तूर्णं विद्ध्वा प्राणान्ररास सः ॥

meaning.en: Parrying his enemies' weapons with weapons on every side, Arjuna quickly pierced them with many arrows and drew from them cries.

verses.text:
छिन्नत्रिवेणुचक्राक्षान्हतयोधाश्वसारथीन् ।
विध्वस्तायुधतूणीरान्समुन्मथितकेतनान् ॥

meaning.en: Chariots with the triple-jointed pole, wheels and axles cut, with warriors, horses and charioteers slain, weapons and quivers shattered, banners torn down,

verses.text:
संछिन्नयोक्त्ररश्मीकान्वित्रिवेणून्विकूबरान् ।
विध्वस्तबन्धुरयुगान्विशस्तायुधमण्डलान् ।
रथान्विशकलीकुर्वन्महाभ्राणीव मारुतः ॥

meaning.en: reins and traces cut, front-boards, yokes and rails broken, seats and yokes smashed and weapon-circles cut, he shattered like a wind scattering great clouds.

verses.text:
विस्मापयन्प्रेक्षणीयं द्विषातां भयवर्धनम् ।
महारथसहस्रस्य समं कर्मार्जुनोऽकरोत् ॥

meaning.en: Astonishing to behold and increasing his enemies' fear, Arjuna did the work of a thousand great chariot-fighters.

verses.text:
सिद्धदेवर्षिसंघाश्च चारणाश्चैव तुष्टुवुः ।
देवदुन्दुभयो नेदुः पुष्पवर्षाणि चापतन् ।
केशवार्जुनयोर्मूर्ध्नि प्राह वाक्चाशरीरिणी ॥

meaning.en: Hosts of perfected beings, divine sages and charanas praised him; heavenly drums sounded and flowers rained down; and a bodiless voice spoke over the heads of Keshava and Arjuna:

verses.text:
चन्द्रार्कानिलवह्नीनां कान्तिदीप्तिबलद्युतीः ।
यौ सदा बिभ्रतुर्वीरौ ताविमौ केशवार्जुनौ ॥

meaning.en: "These two, Keshava and Arjuna, always bear the beauty, brilliance, strength and splendour of the moon, sun, wind and fire.

verses.text:
ब्रह्मेशानाविवाजय्यौ वीरावेकरथे स्थितौ ।
सर्वभूतवरौ वीरौ नरनारायणावुभौ ॥

meaning.en: Two unconquerable heroes like Brahma and Ishana, standing on one chariot, best of all beings, they are Nara and Narayana."

verses.text:
इत्येतन्महदाश्चर्यं दृष्ट्वा श्रुत्वा च भारत ।
अश्वत्थामा सुसंयत्तः कृष्णावभ्यद्रवद्रणे ॥

meaning.en: Having seen and heard this great wonder, O Bharata, Ashvatthama, well prepared, rushed in the battle at Krishna and Arjuna.

verses.text:
अथ पाण्डवमस्यन्तं यमकालान्तकाञ्शरान् ।
सेषुणा पाणिनाहूय हसन्द्रौणिरथाब्रवीत् ॥

meaning.en: Then Drona's son, laughing, calling to the Pandava who was shooting arrows like Yama, Time and the Ender, with bow and arrow in hand, said:

verses.text:
यदि मां मन्यसे वीर प्राप्तमर्हमिवातिथिम् ।
ततः सर्वात्मनाद्य त्वं युद्धातिथ्यं प्रयच्छ मे ॥

meaning.en: "If you think of me, hero, as a worthy guest who has arrived, then today with all your heart give me the hospitality of battle."

verses.text:
एवमाचार्यपुत्रेण समाहूतो युयुत्सया ।
बहु मेनेऽर्जुनोऽऽत्मानमिदं चाह जनार्दनम् ॥

meaning.en: Thus challenged by the teacher's son, eager to fight, Arjuna thought himself honoured and said to Janardana:

verses.text:
संशप्तकाश्च मे वध्या द्रौणिराह्वयते च माम् ।
यदत्रानन्तरं प्राप्तं प्रशाधि त्वं महाभुज ॥

meaning.en: "The Samshaptakas are to be killed by me, and Drona's son is challenging me. Tell me, strong-armed one, what should come next here."

verses.text:
एवमुक्तोऽवहत्पार्थं कृष्णो द्रोणात्मजान्तिकम् ।
जैत्रेण विधिनाहूतं वायुरिन्द्रमिवाध्वरे ॥

meaning.en: Thus addressed, Krishna carried Partha to the teacher's son, as Vayu brings Indra to a sacrifice when summoned by the rite of victory.

verses.text:
तमामन्त्र्यैकमनसा केशवो द्रौणिमब्रवीत् ।
अश्वत्थामन्स्थिरो भूत्वा प्रहराशु सहस्व च ॥

meaning.en: Addressing him with undivided mind, Keshava said to Drona's son: "Ashvatthama, be steady, strike quickly and endure.

verses.text:
निर्वेष्टुं भर्तृपिण्डं हि कालोऽयमुपजीविनाम् ।
सूक्ष्मो विवादो विप्राणां स्थूलौ क्षात्रौ जयाजयौ ॥

meaning.en: This is the time for dependents to discharge what they owe to their master's bread. The disputes of brahmanas are subtle; the victory or defeat of kshatriyas is gross.

verses.text:
यां न संक्षमसे मोहाद्दिव्यां पार्थस्य सत्क्रियाम् ।
तामाप्तुमिच्छन्युध्यस्व स्थिरो भूत्वाद्य पाण्डवम् ॥

meaning.en: The divine honour done to Partha that you cannot bear out of delusion, fight today to win that, standing firm against the Pandava."

verses.text:
इत्युक्तो वासुदेवेन तथेत्युक्त्वा द्विजोत्तमः ।
विव्याध केशवं षष्ट्या नाराचैरर्जुनं त्रिभिः ॥

meaning.en: Thus addressed by Vasudeva, the best of brahmanas said "So be it" and pierced Keshava with sixty iron arrows and Arjuna with three.

verses.text:
तस्यार्जुनः सुसंक्रुद्धस्त्रिभिर्भल्लैः शरासनम् ।
चिच्छेदाथान्यदादत्त द्रौणिर्घोरतरं धनुः ॥

meaning.en: Arjuna, very angry, cut his bow with three bhallas; Drona's son then took another, more terrible bow.

verses.text:
सज्यं कृत्वा निमेषात्तद्विव्याधार्जुनकेशवौ ।
त्रिभिः शरैर्वासुदेवं सहस्रेण च पाण्डवम् ॥

meaning.en: Stringing it in an instant, he pierced Arjuna and Keshava, Vasudeva with three arrows and the Pandava with a thousand.

verses.text:
ततः शरसहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च ।
ससृजे द्रौणिरायस्तः संस्तभ्य च रणेऽर्जुनम् ॥

meaning.en: Then Drona's son, exerting himself, loosed thousands, tens of thousands and millions of arrows, holding Arjuna fast in the battle.

verses.text:
इषुधेर्धनुषो ज्याया अङ्गुलीभ्यश्च मारिष ।
बाह्वोः कराभ्यामुरसो वदनघ्राणनेत्रतः ॥

meaning.en: From his quiver, his bow, his string, his fingers, O lord, from his arms and hands, chest, mouth, nose and eyes,

verses.text:
कर्णाभ्यां शिरसोऽङ्गेभ्यो लोमवर्त्मभ्य एव च ।
रथध्वजेभ्यश्च शरा निष्पेतुर्ब्रह्मवादिनः ॥

meaning.en: from his ears, head and limbs, even from the pores of his hair and from his chariot banners, arrows flew forth, proclaiming the Veda.

verses.text:
शरजालेन महता विद्ध्वा केशवपाण्डवौ ।
ननाद मुदितो द्रौणिर्महामेघौघनिस्वनः ॥

meaning.en: Having pierced Keshava and the Pandava with a great net of arrows, Drona's son roared in delight with a sound like a great mass of clouds.

verses.text:
तस्य नानदतः श्रुत्वा पाण्डवोऽच्युतमब्रवीत् ।
पश्य माधव दौरात्म्यं द्रोणपुत्रस्य मां प्रति ॥

meaning.en: Hearing him roar, the Pandava said to Achyuta: "See, Madhava, the wickedness of Drona's son toward me.

verses.text:
वधप्राप्तौ मन्यते नौ प्रवेश्य शरवेश्मनि ।
एषोऽस्य हन्मि संकल्पं शिक्षया च बलेन च ॥

meaning.en: He thinks that, having brought us into a house of arrows, we have met our end. Now I will destroy his purpose by skill and strength."

verses.text:
अश्वत्थाम्नः शरानस्तांश्छित्त्वैकैकं त्रिधा त्रिधा ।
व्यधमद्भरतश्रेष्ठो नीहारमिव मारुतः ॥

meaning.en: The best of Bharatas cut each of Ashvatthama's arrows in three and scattered them, like the wind scattering mist.

verses.text:
ततः संशप्तकान्भूयः साश्वसूतरथद्विपान् ।
ध्वजपत्तिगणानुग्रैर्बाणैर्विव्याध पाण्डवः ॥

meaning.en: Then the Pandava again pierced the Samshaptakas with fierce arrows, with their horses, charioteers, chariots, elephants, banners and foot-soldiers.

verses.text:
ये ये ददृशिरे तत्र यद्यद्रूपं यथा यथा ।
ते ते तत्तच्छरैर्व्याप्तं मेनिरेऽऽत्मानमेव च ॥

meaning.en: Whatever each saw there, in whatever form and manner, each thought both himself and that thing covered with arrows.

verses.text:
ते गाण्डीवप्रणुदिता नानारूपाः पतत्रिणः ।
क्रोशे साग्रे स्थितान्घ्नन्ति द्विपांश्च पुरुषान्रणे ॥

meaning.en: Driven by Gandiva, arrows of many shapes killed in the battle those standing at a distance of a krosha and more, both elephants and men.

verses.text:
भल्लैश्छिन्नाः कराः पेतुः करिणां मदकर्षिणाम् ।
छिन्ना यथा परशुभिः प्रवृद्धाः शरदि द्रुमाः ॥

meaning.en: Hands of rutting elephants, cut off with bhallas, fell as lofty trees fall in autumn when cut with axes.

verses.text:
पश्चात्तु शैलवत्पेतुस्ते गजाः सह सादिभिः ।
वज्रिवज्रप्रमथिता यथैवाद्रिचयास्तथा ॥

meaning.en: Afterwards those elephants with their riders fell like mountains, like heaps of rock crushed by the thunderbolt-wielder's bolt.

verses.text:
गन्धर्वनगराकारान्विधिवत्कल्पितान्रथान् ।
विनीतजवनान्युक्तानास्थितान्युद्धदुर्मदान् ॥

meaning.en: Chariots that looked like gandharva cities, properly arranged, with trained and yoked horses, mounted by heroes wild for battle,

verses.text:
शरैर्विशकलीकुर्वन्नमित्रानभ्यवीवृषत् ।
अलंकृतानश्वसादीन्पत्तींश्चाहन्धनंजयः ॥

meaning.en: he broke to pieces with arrows and rained on his enemies. Dhananjaya struck down well-adorned horsemen and foot-soldiers.

verses.text:
धनंजययुगान्तार्कः संशप्तकमहार्णवम् ।
व्यशोषयत दुःशोषं तीव्रैः शरगभस्तिभिः ॥

meaning.en: Dhananjaya, like the sun of the end of the age, dried up the ocean of Samshaptakas, hard to dry, with the fierce rays of his arrows.

verses.text:
पुनर्द्रौणिमहाशैलं नाराचैः सूर्यसंनिभैः ।
निर्बिभेद महावेगैस्त्वरन्वज्रीव पर्वतम् ॥

meaning.en: Again, hurrying, he pierced the great mountain that was Drona's son with iron arrows like the sun, like the thunderbolt-wielder piercing a mountain.

verses.text:
तमाचार्यसुतः क्रुद्धः साश्वयन्तारमाशुगैः ।
युयुत्सुर्नाशकद्योद्धुं पार्थस्तानन्तराच्छिनत् ॥

meaning.en: The teacher's son, angry and eager to fight, could not fight with the arrows aimed at him with his horses and charioteer, as Partha cut them midway.

verses.text:
ततः परमसंक्रुद्धः काण्डकोशानवासृजत् ।
अश्वत्थामाभिरूपाय गृहानतिथये यथा ॥

meaning.en: Then, in the highest rage, he loosed arrows from quivers, as one offers a house to a worthy guest.

verses.text:
अथ संशप्तकांस्त्यक्त्वा पाण्डवो द्रौणिमभ्ययात् ।
अपाङ्क्तेयमिव त्यक्त्वा दाता पाङ्क्तेयमर्थिनम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the Pandava, leaving the Samshaptakas, went to Drona's son, as a giver would leave an unworthy guest and go to a worthy suppliant.

verses.text:
ततः समभवद्युद्धं शुक्राङ्गिरसवर्चसोः ।
नक्षत्रमभितो व्योम्नि शुक्राङ्गिरसयोरिव ॥

meaning.en: Then a battle took place between two of the brilliance of Shukra and Angiras, like that of the planets Shukra and Angiras in the sky near a constellation.

verses.text:
संतापयन्तावन्योन्यं दीप्तैः शरगभस्तिभिः ।
लोकत्रासकरावास्तां विमार्गस्थौ ग्रहाविव ॥

meaning.en: Scorching each other with bright rays of arrows, they stood terrifying the world like two planets out of course.

verses.text:
ततोऽविध्यद्भ्रुवोर्मध्ये नाराचेनार्जुनो भृशम् ।
स तेन विबभौ द्रौणिरूर्ध्वरश्मिर्यथा रविः ॥

meaning.en: Then Arjuna struck him hard between the brows with an iron arrow, and by it Drona's son shone like the sun with upturned rays.

verses.text:
अथ कृष्णौ शरशतैरश्वत्थाम्नार्दितौ भृशम् ।
सरश्मिजालनिकरौ युगान्तार्काविवासतुः ॥

meaning.en: Then the two Krishnas, tormented by hundreds of arrows from Ashvatthama, looked like the two suns of the end of the age with masses of rays.

verses.text:
ततोऽर्जुनः सर्वतोधारमस्त्र-
मवासृजद्वासुदेवाभिगुप्तः ।
द्रौणायनिं चाभ्यहनत्पृषत्कै-
र्वज्राग्निवैवस्वतदण्डकल्पैः ॥

meaning.en: Then Arjuna, guarded by Vasudeva, loosed a weapon that cuts on all sides and struck Drona's son with arrows like the thunderbolt, fire and the rod of Vivasvat's son.

verses.text:
स केशवं चार्जुनं चातितेजा
विव्याध मर्मस्वतिरौद्रकर्मा ।
बाणैः सुमुक्तैरतितीव्रवेगै-
र्यैराहतो मृत्युरपि व्यथेत ॥

meaning.en: Of great fury and most terrible deed, he pierced Keshava and Arjuna in their vital parts with well-loosed arrows of very fierce speed, by which even Death would have been pained.

verses.text:
द्रौणेरिषूनर्जुनः संनिवार्य
व्यायच्छतस्तद्द्विगुणैः सुपुङ्खैः ।
तं साश्वसूतध्वजमेकवीर-
मावृत्य संशप्तकसैन्यमार्छत् ॥

meaning.en: Arjuna, warding off Drona's son's arrows with feathered arrows twice as many against him as he strove, covered that lone hero with horses, charioteer and banner and then turned to the Samshaptaka army.

verses.text:
धनूंषि बाणानिषुधीर्धनुर्ज्याः
पाणीन्भुजान्पाणिगतं च शस्त्रम् ।
छत्राणि केतूंस्तुरगानथैषां
वस्त्राणि माल्यान्यथ भूषणानि ॥

meaning.en: Bows, arrows, quivers, bowstrings, hands, arms and weapons in hands, umbrellas, banners, horses, their garments, garlands and ornaments,

verses.text:
चर्माणि वर्माणि मनोरथांश्च
प्रियाणि सर्वाणि शिरांसि चैव ।
चिच्छेद पार्थो द्विषतां प्रमुक्तै-
र्बाणैः स्थितानामपराङ्मुखानाम् ॥

meaning.en: shields, armour, hopes, all that was dear, and heads, Partha cut off with loosed arrows from his enemies as they stood without turning back.

verses.text:
सुकल्पिताः स्यन्दनवाजिनागाः
समास्थिताः कृतयत्नैर्नृवीरैः ।
पार्थेरितैर्बाणगणैर्निरस्ता-
स्तैरेव सार्धं नृवरैर्निपेतुः ॥

meaning.en: Chariots, horses and elephants, well arrayed and occupied by heroic men who strove, were cast down by the flights of arrows Partha sent, and fell with those best of men.

verses.text:
पद्मार्कपूर्णेन्दुसमाननानि
किरीटमालामुकुटोत्कटानि ।
भल्लार्धचन्द्रक्षुरहिंसितानि
प्रपेतुरुर्व्यां नृशिरांस्यजस्रम् ॥

meaning.en: Heads with faces like lotus, sun and full moon, adorned with diadems, garlands and crowns, cut by bhallas, half-moon arrows and razor-arrows, fell without ceasing to the earth.

verses.text:
अथ द्विपैर्देवपतिद्विपाभै-
र्देवारिदर्पोल्बणमन्युदर्पैः ।
कलिङ्गवङ्गाङ्गनिषादवीरा
जिघांसवः पाण्डवमभ्यधावन् ॥

meaning.en: Then the heroes of Kalinga, Vanga, Anga and Nishada, eager to kill, with elephants like Indra's elephant, wild with the pride of fury like the foes of the gods, rushed at the Pandava.

verses.text:
तेषां द्विपानां विचकर्त पार्थो
वर्माणि मर्माणि करान्नियन्तॄन् ।
ध्वजाः पताकाश्च ततः प्रपेतु-
र्वज्राहतानीव गिरेः शिरांसि ॥

meaning.en: Partha cut the armour, vital parts, trunks and drivers of those elephants; then banners and flags fell like peaks of a mountain struck by lightning.

verses.text:
तेषु प्ररुग्णेषु गुरोस्तनूजं
बाणैः किरीटी नवसूर्यवर्णैः ।
प्रच्छादयामास महाभ्रजालै-
र्वायुः समुद्युक्तमिवांशुमन्तम् ॥

meaning.en: When they were broken, Kiritin covered the teacher's son with arrows the colour of the new sun, as wind covers the sun with great masses of cloud.

verses.text:
ततोऽर्जुनेषूनिषुभिर्निरस्य
द्रौणिः शरैरर्जुनवासुदेवौ ।
प्रच्छादयित्व दिवि चन्द्रसूर्यौ
ननाद सोऽम्भोद इवातपान्ते ॥

meaning.en: Then Drona's son, driving off Arjuna's arrows with arrows, covered Arjuna and Vasudeva with shafts as if covering moon and sun in the sky, and roared like a cloud at summer's end.

verses.text:
तमर्जुनस्तांश्च पुनस्त्वदीया-
नभ्यर्दितस्तैरविकृत्तशस्त्रैः ।
बाणान्धकारं सहसैव कृत्वा
विव्याध सर्वानिषुभिः सुपुङ्खैः ॥

meaning.en: Again Arjuna, though attacked by him and by your soldiers with unbroken weapons, suddenly made a darkness of arrows and pierced them all with well-feathered arrows.

verses.text:
नाप्याददत्संदधन्नैव मुञ्च-
न्बाणान्रणेऽदृश्यत सव्यसाची ।
हतांश्च नागांस्तुरगान्पदाती-
न्संस्यूतदेहान्ददृशू रथांश्च ॥

meaning.en: Savyasachin was not seen taking, aiming or loosing arrows in the battle; only elephants, horses, foot-soldiers and chariots were seen slain, their bodies stitched through.

verses.text:
संधाय नाराचवरान्दशाशु
द्रौणिस्त्वरन्नेकमिवोत्ससर्ज ।
तेषां च पञ्चार्जुनमभ्यविध्य-
न्पञ्चाच्युतं निर्बिभिदुः सुमुक्ताः ॥

meaning.en: Drona's son, hurrying, fitted ten fine iron arrows and shot them at once as if one; five of them pierced Arjuna and five pierced Achyuta, well loosed.

verses.text:
तैराहतौ सर्वमनुष्यमुख्या-
वसृक्क्षरन्तौ धनदेन्द्रकल्पौ ।
समाप्तविद्येन यथाभिभूतौ
हतौ स्विदेतौ किमु मेनिरेऽन्ये ॥

meaning.en: Struck by them, the two chief of all men, streaming blood, like Kubera and Indra, were as if defeated by one who had finished his learning; what else could others have thought but that they were killed?

verses.text:
अथार्जुनं प्राह दशार्हनाथः
प्रमाद्यसे किं जहि योधमेतम् ।
कुर्याद्धि दोषं समुपेक्षितोऽसौ
कष्टो भवेद्व्याधिरिवाक्रियावान् ॥

meaning.en: Then the lord of the Dasharhas said to Arjuna: "Why are you careless? Kill this warrior. If ignored, he will do harm; he will be painful like a disease left untreated."

verses.text:
तथेति चोक्त्वाच्युतमप्रमादी
द्रौणिं प्रयत्नादिषुभिस्ततक्ष ।
छित्त्वाश्वरश्मींस्तुरगानविध्य-
त्ते तं रणादूहुरतीव दूरम् ॥

meaning.en: Saying "So be it," Arjuna, now careful, with effort shaved Drona's son with arrows; cutting his reins, he pierced his horses, and they carried him far from the battle.

verses.text:
आवृत्य नेयेष पुनस्तु युद्धं
पार्थेन सार्धं मतिमान्विमृश्य ।
जानञ्जयं नियतं वृष्णिवीरे
धनंजये चाङ्गिरसां वरिष्ठः ॥

meaning.en: Having turned back, he did not wish to renew the battle with Partha, for the wise best of the Angirasas, reflecting, knew that victory was assured for the Vrishni hero and Dhananjaya.

verses.text:
प्रतीपकाये तु रणादश्वत्थाम्नि हृते हयैः ।
मन्त्रौषधिक्रियादानैर्व्याधौ देहादिवाहृते ॥

meaning.en: When Ashvatthama had been carried away from the battle by his horses, like a disease driven out of the body by mantras, herbs, rites and gifts,

verses.text:
संशप्तकानभिमुखौ प्रयातौ केशवार्जुनौ ।
वातोद्धूतपताकेन स्यन्दनेनौघनादिना ॥

meaning.en: Keshava and Arjuna went on facing the Samshaptakas in a chariot whose flags were blown by the wind and which rumbled like a flood.
